name: Brazilian Moqueca Fish Stew with Rice

components.name: Moqueca Fish Stew
steps: Toss 700 g fish cubes with half the lime juice, 3 g salt and a little black pepper; leave for 10 minutes in the refrigerator.
Heat olive oil in a deep sauté pan and soften onion, garlic and red pepper.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, cumin, paprika, cayenne and sugar; simmer to build a fragrant sauce.
Pour in coconut milk and fish stock, simmer gently until sauce thickens slightly; add fish cubes in a single layer.
Cook fish gently to 63 C, finish with cilantro and remaining lime, then pack stew and rice separately.

components.name: White Rice
steps: Cook the 280 g white rice in the measured water, rest covered, and cool promptly if preparing ahead.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
RecipeTin Eats fish stew adapted with larger fish quantity and measured dry rice to create four complete lunches/dinners.
Storing & reheating: Freeze stew and rice separately and use a gentle simmer for reheating; coconut sauce may separate slightly.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Fish stew — plan for days 1-3; freeze later-week portions.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
